names.en: Two Eggs, One Shared Pot (place-aware boil)
names.es: Dos Huevos, Una Olla Compartida (hervido consciente del lugar)

metadata.notes: Built 2026-08-16 as the concrete, end-to-end proof for ROADMAP.md's 'Heat as a shared, time-varying property of a PLACE' entry, closing the exact sentence that entry used to describe the gap: 'Two ingredients simmering in the same pot right now get independent, unlinked applyAction calls each carrying their own waterTempC/durationSeconds guess, not one shared temperature.' Both eggs here are PLACE_IN'd into the identical placeId ('pot-1'), which is HEATed exactly ONCE — both BOIL steps then reference that same placeId, and src/recipe-runner.ts's assertPlaceReady requires the place to genuinely be at boiling point before either BOIL is allowed to proceed, not just trusting a per-call parameter. Run `npm run recipe -- two_eggs_shared_pot` (or read scripts/validate.ts's simulation output) and check the log: the HEAT_PLACE line names both egg-1 and egg-2 as 'shared by', at the SAME temperature, from ONE heating step, not two.
metadata.startMethodNote: startMethod: 'boiling_start' on both BOIL steps is not just informational here the way boil.json's own startMethodNote otherwise describes it — it's now the LITERALLY TRUE description of what happened: HEAT_PLACE ran to completion (reaching 100°C) BEFORE either PLACE_IN step, so both eggs really did go into already-boiling water. See scripts/ for a capability-test script contrasting this against the cold_start order (PLACE_IN before HEAT_PLACE) using the identical mechanism.
metadata.scopeNote: This recipe deliberately does not attempt PEEL/SALT — kept minimal and focused on proving the shared-place mechanism specifically, not a complete serving recipe; see data/recipes/soft-boiled-egg.json for the fuller single-egg version this reuses BOIL/SHOCK's exact same durationSeconds/yolkDoneness values from.
